goal: Find how Enron is connected to the invention or spread of weather derivatives: the first deal, where they came to be traded, and the companies and people involved.

nodes.title: Enron
nodes.note: Enron’s EnronOnline platform offered weather risk management products, showing the company’s involvement in trading weather derivatives, but details on the first deal, trading venues, and key participants are not given here.

nodes.title: Weather derivative
nodes.note: The page identifies the first weather derivative deal (July 1996, Aquila Energy structuring a dual‑commodity hedge for Consolidated Edison), notes OTC trading began in 1997, and that the CME launched exchange‑traded weather futures in 1999; it also mentions Enron’s early exploration via EnronOnline.

nodes.title: Aquila, Inc.
nodes.note: Aquila Inc. (formerly Aquila Energy) structured the first weather‑derivative transaction in July 1996, a dual‑commodity hedge for Consolidated Edison, establishing Aquila’s pioneering role in the market.

nodes.title: Enron scandal
nodes.note: The Enron scandal page shows Enron’s extensive use of derivatives and its accounting practices (reporting full trade value as revenue), confirming the company’s deep involvement in derivative markets but provides no specific details on weather‑derivative deals or trading venues.

nodes.title: Futures contract
nodes.note: The futures contract page provides general background on futures contracts, explaining they are exchange‑traded instruments distinct from over‑the‑counter forwards, which is relevant because early weather‑derivative deals were OTC before CME introduced exchange‑traded weather futures, but it adds no specific Enron or weather‑derivative details.

nodes.title: Derivatives market
nodes.note: The Derivatives market page provides general background on OTC vs exchange‑traded derivatives, confirming that early weather‑derivative contracts were OTC before later moving to exchanges, but adds no specific Enron or weather‑derivative details.

nodes.title: Futures exchange
nodes.note: The Futures exchange page provides general background on how futures exchanges operate and standardize contracts, but does not add specific information about weather derivatives or Enron’s involvement, only contextualizing exchange‑traded derivatives.

nodes.title: Swap (finance)
nodes.note: The swap page explains that swaps are primarily over‑the‑counter contracts, first publicly disclosed in 1981 (IBM‑World Bank), highlighting the OTC nature of early derivative deals like the initial weather‑derivative transaction.

nodes.title: Structured product
nodes.note: The structured product page explains that such products are pre‑packaged derivatives but provides no specific information on weather derivatives or Enron’s role in them.

nodes.title: Derivative (finance)
nodes.note: The Derivative (finance) page gives a broad overview of derivatives, defines OTC vs exchange‑traded contracts, and mentions weather derivatives as an example of exposure where the underlying isn’t tradable, but provides no specific details on Enron’s role, the first weather‑derivative deal, or the trading venues or participants.

nodes.title: Trading room
nodes.note: The Trading room page describes the front‑office environment where electronic trading (e.g., EnronOnline) occurs, but provides no specific details about Enron’s weather‑derivative transactions, the first deal, or the people involved.

nodes.title: Climate finance
nodes.note: The Climate finance page discusses broad climate‑related financing mechanisms but provides no specific information about Enron, the first weather‑derivative deal, trading venues, or the individuals involved.
